Item / Decision: Dolly surface for the opening push: run on concrete as-is vs. lay dance floors vs. lay tracks + remove in VFX
Options / Notes: Path to the bench is concrete with a possible slight slope. (a) roll on concrete = shake risk; (b) dance floors; (c) tracks removed in VFX. Sam: scout whether the concrete is smooth enough to roll without tracks before committing to VFX removal. Decide on-site.

Item / Decision: Writing legibility over-the-shoulder is not a priority
Options / Notes: On a ~30mm wide/medium lens legibility is limited; team agreed seeing that he is writing is enough - the voiceover carries the content.

Item / Decision: Pedestal vs. tilt-down to the notebook before the pan-right to the woman
Options / Notes: Camera drops to the notebook, pans right across the ground (leaves / wind), reveals the woman's legs, then tilts up to finish on her sitting on a bollard. Pedestal-or-tilt not locked.

Item / Decision: Woman sits on a bollard, not a parallel bench
Options / Notes: Script originally placed her on a parallel bench; changed to a bollard to avoid a cheesy symmetry.

Item / Decision: Deliberate 180-degree-rule break for the conversation coverage - test before committing
Options / Notes: Man's angle: on-axis side profile. Woman's angle: from behind and slightly to the side, only half her face. Goal: the audience never has spatial certainty about where she is relative to him (real / imagined / ghostly). The unconventional cutting may feel jarring - plan to test it in practice first.

Item / Decision: Sparing full-spatial establishing shot
Options / Notes: One shot that reveals both characters in frame to establish their relative positions; used sparingly so the spatial ambiguity is not fully resolved. Placement within the scene still TBD.

Item / Decision: Woman's exit and re-entry direction
Options / Notes: She walks off (likely camera right); camera pans right across nature without her; she reappears from the same or the opposite side. Intent: naturalistic, not ghostly, but the audience briefly loses track of her. Leaning naturalistic; not finalized.

Item / Decision: Wind / fan rig for the paper fly-away
Options / Notes: Friends recruited to engineer a wind/fan rig so the paper looks genuinely caught in the wind, not just dropped. May also grab a shot of the paper in the air for editorial flexibility. Possible cut to the woman: 'It has a rebellious turn of mind,' + footsteps chasing the paper. See reference-docs/ufi-wind-rig-responsibility-matrix.

Item / Decision: Scene 1 is the most technically complex / shot-dense sequence (~8-9 shots, ~3.5 script pages)
Options / Notes: Flagged as the shot-count and time risk for the schedule. Track against the 10-12 shots/day guidance.

Item / Decision: Shoulder rig vs. static-with-slight-reframe to follow the boy walking
Options / Notes: After the boy hears his name and stands, the camera pedestals up with him then follows. Shoulder rig is preferred for the naturalistic feel and time efficiency, but conflicts with the film's settled aesthetic. Not chosen.

Item / Decision: Memory-scene look: higher frame rate + a slight colour-grade shift
Options / Notes: Memory scenes (2 & 4) should read slightly different from the main timeline - shoot at a higher fps and slow ~0.9x in post, plus a subtle grade variation (not black-and-white). Confirm the approach with Alex on the Monday scout.

Item / Decision: Tree deliberately framed on the right for a later match cut
Options / Notes: Boy digs in the dirt near a large tree positioned frame-right; it rhymes with the woman's background position in Scene 3's opening.

Item / Decision: Split the following shot into two (before / after the cut to the boy) with a closer reframe on the return
Options / Notes: Dolly follows the man & woman from behind on tracks (the road surface allows it). They pause, look up; the camera tilts up but cuts before revealing what they see.

Item / Decision: Where to cut the upward tilt
Options / Notes: Plan is to tilt all the way up and decide the exact cut point in editing.

Item / Decision: Man-picks-up-paper: the woman's background position echoes the memory-shot tree
Options / Notes: Static shot; paper lands on the road, the man enters and leans to pick it up, the woman enters and walks to a background position that visually rhymes with the tree. The paper prop must match Scene 1's fly-away exactly (same fold / crumple).

Item / Decision: Tilt-angle continuity between Scene 3's up-look and Scene 4's opening
Options / Notes: The cut must pick up at roughly the same tilt angle or the transition jumps. May be partially fixable in editing. Leading approach: Scene 4 starts high on the trees and tilts DOWN to reveal the boy (Option A), rather than continuing the upward tilt (Option B, which risks a compositional mismatch since the camera would be above the boy).

Item / Decision: Higher frame rate (shoot 30fps, deliver 24fps) for a subtle slow-motion
Options / Notes: Not full slow-motion (60fps would be too extreme). To be confirmed with Sam and Alex.

Item / Decision: High-angle-looking-down composition, largely static
Options / Notes: Preferred: a high angle down on the boy walking through the forest, on uneven downhill terrain. Static, given the difficulty of moving equipment at height. Boy hears his name, looks around briefly, walks off screen.

Item / Decision: Shafi to draw a revised frame showing the trees-first / tilt-down composition
Options / Notes: Action item from 9/2 - needed for the storyboard set.

Item / Decision: Add a slight dolly move to the 'painting shot'
Options / Notes: Shot 2: the woman looks up (not at the man - as if something made her stop), the man enters screen-right and freezes; held mostly static. Action item: annotate the slight dolly on the shot list. The static frame constrains composition flexibility.

Item / Decision: Getting a dolly up the staircase
Options / Notes: The Fisher dolly up a staircase may be impossible. Alternatives: a smaller rental dolly from Bad Dog, or a shoulder rig for that shot only. The shoulder rig gives an unsettled, hovering look inconsistent with the Tarkovsky-influenced aesthetic.

Item / Decision: Ishmam to hand-draw rough compositions for shots 4, 5, 6, 7
Options / Notes: So Shafi can generate AI reference images. Shot 6 = walking down stairs. Shot 7 = wide shot, characters walking left-to-right in a park-like setting, functions as an insert over continuing dialogue.

Item / Decision: Location for the insert wide - park-ish but not overtly, and must match the previous location
Options / Notes: Wide shot of the characters walking left-to-right; needs to read as park-like without being obviously a park, and must visually match the preceding location.

Item / Decision: Seating location + elevation for the woman/man depth composition
Options / Notes: Woman sits low (log / stump height, not bollard height, which puts her near standing height); the man is positioned lower on a slope so their faces sit at a similar elevation for the pan. Favoured: the area where Ishmam & Ishiko were at different elevations. Rejected: the cut-off stump near the first park bench (feels like returning to an earlier location).

Item / Decision: Source or bring a wooden stump as a production-design element
Options / Notes: May need to bring a wooden stump to location for the woman's seat.

Item / Decision: Lens choice for the dolly-in -> tilt-down -> pan-to-man
Options / Notes: The dolly pushes in on the woman, tilts down to the book / hands, then pans left to the man's face at roughly the same elevation. Must keep the man's face in frame through the pan - a longer lens risks clipping it. Dolly tracks needed on grass.

Item / Decision: Whether to simplify Scene 5 if the schedule tightens
Options / Notes: Scene 5 is the longest / most complex scene and the identified candidate for cuts under schedule pressure.

Item / Decision: Scene 5 is the longest scene (multi-location, most dialogue) - roughly 9 shots / 200 words
Options / Notes: The other long / complex scene alongside Scene 1. Watch shot count and the time cost of long takes.

Item / Decision: Pedestal vs. tilt-up from the forest floor to reveal the bed
Options / Notes: A low-to-high move revealing the bed; the boy stops at the edge. Pedestal-or-tilt not locked.

Item / Decision: Can the location be shot on a tripod without a dolly?
Options / Notes: The location is the far end of the interview woods area; it may be tripod-able. Needs scout confirmation - ties into the dolly-transport problem.

Item / Decision: One continuous shot vs. cutting to the fabric-grip insert
Options / Notes: Preferred: shoot the whole jumping sequence in one shot (camera tilts up over the first 1-2 jumps, holds at sky level, boy jumps in and out of frame, spins mid-air, camera tilts back down). If the dolly can't reach the location or it is too technically difficult, cut to a close-up insert of the boy gripping the bed fabric as a natural break.

Item / Decision: Camera parallel to the bed vs. bed angled with the boy parallel to camera
Options / Notes: To be tested on location.

Item / Decision: Add the 'boy gripping bed fabric' insert to the shot list
Options / Notes: Contingency insert if the one-shot can't be executed. Action item from 9/2.

Item / Decision: Ruckenfigur -> slow pan to the woman near the tree line
Options / Notes: Boy seen from behind looks back, camera holds, then pans slowly to the woman standing almost against the trees in the distance.

Item / Decision: What to cut to between the argument climax and the Tarkovsky pan
Options / Notes: A cut is needed between the argument and the pan. Cutting to the boy risks giving him a premature conclusion. Leading candidate: cut to the soil / earth from the earlier forest scene (no boy, just the ground he was digging).

Item / Decision: Bollard placement for the pan's first stop - road & houses visible in the background
Options / Notes: The pan opens near where the couple sits and moves across the field; the first stop is the now-empty bollards. Shooting back toward the real bollards shows the road and houses. Options: (a) move the bollards to a different position in the field (symbolic / supernatural placement) or (b) include the bollards only briefly before panning to the couple.

Item / Decision: Zoom lens for the pan (zoomed in at the start, zooms out for depth)
Options / Notes: The Tarkovsky reference uses a zoom lens and layered composition (grass / dirt / trees / secondary trees / sun). Need to confirm a zoom lens is available; this conflicts with the same-lens-per-sequence rule and needs thought.

Item / Decision: End the pan on a tilt-down (the reference likely uses a crane)
Options / Notes: Their version will use a tilt rather than a crane move.

Item / Decision: Actors must fully memorise lines for this scene (single static shot, dialogue-heavy)
Options / Notes: Most of the scene is one static shot with heavy dialogue; ADR covers the rest of the film but this scene needs the performance on the day.

Item / Decision: Blocking: the man turns sideways (screen right) at the argument climax, not fully back-to-camera
Options / Notes: Characters sit apart and converse; the woman stands and turns away; the man crosses the implied barrier first, the woman follows.

Item / Decision: Jacket continuity: does the old woman wear the younger woman's jacket?
Options / Notes: The same jacket could imply a generational link (mother's jacket handed down) but risks being too on-the-nose. Leaning toward redressing the old woman entirely.

Item / Decision: Old-woman costume: a granny-style sundress that hangs full-length with a small layer over it
Options / Notes: Separate from the younger woman's clothes. Need Holly's sizing for a fitting reference. Action item: Shafi to brief Ishika.

Item / Decision: Shoot the old-woman shots last of the day
Options / Notes: Holly's old-age makeup process is irreversible for that session.

Item / Decision: Shoot both the side-of-street and the interview locations
Options / Notes: Side-of-street (shot from the far side) confirmed by a Fujifilm photo reference. Shoot both to have options in the edit. The woman is distant enough that makeup detail matters less than the clothing silhouette.

Item / Decision: Build a dedicated insert list for every scene
Options / Notes: Sam regretted not doing this on his own shoot. Nature (light through leaves, wind in grass, leaves on the ground), prop close-ups (notebook, pen, paper, a corner of the dress), walking cutaways, symbolically significant objects as bookends. Lock the specifics on the Monday scout with Alex.

Item / Decision: Keep the total shot count deliberate - currently 29, inserts could push it toward ~40
Options / Notes: Sam: 36 is 'completely fine'; also identify 5-10 nice-to-have bonus shots to attempt only if time permits, without compromising the core story.

Item / Decision: Add closer shots (mediums / close-ups) - scenes 2-4 currently skew wide
Options / Notes: Sam emphasised shot variation for emotional connection, especially in scenes 2-4.

Item / Decision: Same lens for every shot within a sequence
Options / Notes: Consistency rule for pans and tilts. Note the tension with the Scene 7 zoom-lens idea.

Item / Decision: Frame rate: 24fps standard; 30fps for the forest / boy scenes; 60fps rejected
Options / Notes: Allows a subtle slow-down in post for the memory scenes. Confirm with Sam and Alex.

Item / Decision: Dolly tracks required on grass for the outdoor scenes
Options / Notes: Plan the rental and transport accordingly.
